newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CVRD, Ripasa form pulp firm with Nissho. [CORRECTED 17:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CVRD, Ripasa form pulp firm with Nissho. [CORRECTED 17:45 GMT]

text.p: State mining firm Companhia do Vale do Rio Doce has joined with Brazil's Ripasa and Japan's Nissho Iwai Corp in a $960 million deal to create a pulp firm in the norhteastern state of Maranhao, company officials said.

The new company, Celmar Industria de Celulose e Papel, will be Brazil's second largest pulp producer after Aracruz Celulose and is expected to create 3,700 jobs, Celmar's superintendent director Fabio Medeiros said.
"CVRD and Ripasa have a 42.5 percent stake each in Celmar with the remaining 15 percent going to Nissho Iwai Corp," Medeiros said.

The new company will start production in 2001 and aims to produce 500,000 tons of cellulose a year, he said. Celmar's shareholders are financing 40 percent of the joint venture, and Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) and Japan's Eximbank are funding 30 percent each. (Corrects sources of funding).
Annual turnover is estimated at around $320 million and 90 percent of cellulose production is destined for export markets in North America, Europe and Asia, Medeiros said.
